articles.title: How Love Comes to You
articles.highlight: 放弃任何事物——梦想、所爱之人、爱本身——就等于否认生命中那股最不可抑制的搏动。
articles.summary: 这篇文章选自The Marginalian，以诗意笔触探讨爱如何不期而至。它指出生活总在超出人的计划与想象，最狂野的赌注往往就是赢家，而放弃任何事物等于否定生命本身的活力。值得阅读，因为它用温柔而深刻的方式提醒我们保持开放与相信。
articles.failureAnalysis: 核心启示：别因计划与预测而封闭自己，最狂野的赌注往往获胜；放弃梦想或爱就是放弃生命的脉搏。
articles.sourceExcerpt: We spend our days making plans, making promises, making predictions about the possible, and yet the most bewildering thing about life is that its imagination is always greater than that of the living — life keeps surprising us, keeps reminding us that all too often the wildest bet is the winning bet. And all the while, we, living mysteries, keep surprising ourselves. To give up on anything — a dream, a loved one, love itself — is to deny this most irrepressible pulse-beat of being alive.

articles.title: Don't classify. Hallucinate!
articles.selectionReason: AI source passed freshness and evidence-chain gate: Expert analysis
articles.summary: Simon Willison 介绍了 Doug Turnbull 的一个巧妙做法：与其把全部 1856 个标签塞给大模型让它挑选，不如先让模型自由“幻觉”出一些新标签，再用向量嵌入与现有标签库比对，找出最接近的真实标签。这样既省上下文，又能利用模型对语义的理解，为大量未打标的旧内容补齐标签。
articles.failureAnalysis: 关键在于现有标签库需要有可用的嵌入向量，并且模型虚构的标签与真实标签在语义上足够接近，否则检索效果会打折扣。
articles.highlight: 先让模型凭想象输出标签，再用向量嵌入在现有语料中找到最接近的具体标签。
articles.sourceExcerpt: I still have quite a bit of older content on my blog that I never got round to tagging. My blog has 1,856 tags - likely too many to feed to an LLM in one go and say "which of these tags match the following content". Doug Turnbull has a neat solution.

zh.title: 不要分类，让模型“幻觉”出标签
zh.highlight: 先让模型凭想象输出标签，再用向量嵌入在现有语料中找到最接近的具体标签。
zh.summary: Simon Willison 介绍了 Doug Turnbull 的一个巧妙做法：与其把全部 1856 个标签塞给大模型让它挑选，不如先让模型自由“幻觉”出一些新标签，再用向量嵌入与现有标签库比对，找出最接近的真实标签。这样既省上下文，又能利用模型对语义的理解，为大量未打标的旧内容补齐标签。
zh.failureAnalysis: 关键在于现有标签库需要有可用的嵌入向量，并且模型虚构的标签与真实标签在语义上足够接近，否则检索效果会打折扣。

en.highlight: Tell the model to output tags without any details of the existing vocabulary, then use vector embeddings to find the concrete tags closest to the imagined ones.
en.summary: Simon Willison describes Doug Turnbull's neat solution: instead of feeding all 1,856 existing tags to an LLM and asking it to pick matches, let the model freely hallucinate possible tags, then use vector embeddings to find the closest real tags in the corpus. This saves context and leverages semantic understanding, making it practical for tagging older untagged content.
en.failureAnalysis: The key requirement is an embeddable existing tag corpus, and the hallucinated tags need to be semantically close enough to real tags for the matching to work well.
en.title: Don't classify. Hallucinate!
